source_snapshot.items: Test connections between BMC I2C-6 and UPHY0 from second PG548
source_snapshot.procedure: Uses bus5 mux0x71 and0x01 port0, identical to first-PG548 UPHY0 row125, despite row124 using mux0x75 for second PG548.
source_snapshot.criteria: No endpoint oracle or restore; generic artifacts only.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; invents physical probing and misses address contradiction.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Adds state safety but accepts0x71 without reconciling second-PG548 identity.

old_problem: Second-PG548 identity conflicts with copied first-PG548 mux0x71/port0 while sibling row124 assigns second PG548 to0x75; bus mapping, endpoint replies, ownership, bit semantics and exact restoration are also absent.
disposition_reason: ED-03 forbids guessing whether0x71,0x75 or an alias is the OEM target. A safe conditional functional method exists, so static review is complete and RPUC remains, but the state-changing source write cannot run until PID1114953 resolves the cross-row topology conflict.
decision_basis: Read row126/history2517, directly compared rows124-125 and verified baseline row127 plus next pending row128.
Preserved second-PG548 UPHY0 intent and literal0x71/0x01 facts without silently correcting Master.
Flagged that executing the copied command may only repeat first-PG548 row125 coverage.
Required authoritative mux identity, endpoint replies, sibling isolation and exact restoration; rejected physical-only invention.
No candidate mux read/write, blind scan, BMC reset, physical probe or DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: Second PG548 UPHY0 mux-identity and functional path
test_case.purpose: After PID topology resolution, verify UPHY0 reachability through the authoritative second-PG548 mux/port from BMC I2C-6, prove this is not a repeat of first-PG548 row125, and restore routing without service impact.
required_package: PID1114953 authoritative second-PG548 UPHY0 mux/address/port and alias explanation
Reconciliation matrix for rows124-126 and proof I2C-6 maps to bus5
Exact UPHY0 endpoint transactions/replies and timeout/NACK rules
Bus ownership/exclusivity, sibling isolation, original-state restore and BMC recovery
test_case.test_command: Do not execute the source0x71 write. First resolve whether second PG548 is0x71,0x75 or an approved alias. Then capture the authoritative mux byte/ownership, select only the approved port, run PID-defined UPHY0 reads, prove both PG548 identities/isolation, restore the exact byte and revalidate BMC services.
test_case.expected_result: The PID-authoritative second-PG548 UPHY0 endpoints reply within bounds through the resolved mux/port, evidence distinguishes the path from first-PG548, no sibling/service impact occurs, and all routing/readbacks return exactly to baseline.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS or execution while mux identity conflicts. A0x71 ACK alone may duplicate row125. Wrong-device signature, NACK/timeout, sibling impact, mapping ambiguity or incomplete restoration fails/retains Pending; physical photos are not required absent separate approval.
safety_gate: No supplied0x71 write until PID resolves second-PG548 identity.
Authoritative BMC ownership, exclusive access and independent recovery.
Capture original byte at the resolved address and preserve unrelated bits.
One bounded transaction; abort/restore on wrong signature or management degradation.
expected_evidence: PID excerpt resolving second-PG548 mux/address/port and I2C-6/bus5
Rows124-126 topology reconciliation and path-isolation matrix
Approved select/readback plus expected-versus-observed UPHY0 replies
Both-PG548 and sibling-channel health with bus logs
test_case.recovery: Restore the exact authoritative mux byte and verify both PG548 paths plus BMC services. Use independent BMC recovery only for a stuck bus; never test alternate addresses by scanning or retry automatically.

source_conflict.reason: Second-PG548 label conflicts with the repeated first-PG5480x71/0x01 command and row124's0x75 mapping; Criteria also lacks replies.

blocked.reason: A safe conditional procedure can be reviewed; execution is gated by an owner topology decision, so pipeline review continues as RPUC.
